conviction_note: The H1 print is about whether ANA rewrites a full-year plan built on 2H Singapore kerosene of $90 when Aug-Sep averaged about ¥25-26k/bbl (~$160) and the company said at Q1 it would fold Q2 into its 2H assumptions; a trim is more likely than not and the stale IFIS consensus (OP ¥164bn) sits above the ¥150bn plan, but the stock is already ~12% off its post-Q1 level and rose 4.15% on the -31% guide in April, so the lean is small (p_up 45 on abs 3.5 = -0.35) while the findings sum to -1.0; the gap is the 悪材料出尽くし risk, which I keep in p_up rather than in the findings.
bar: Full-year FY2027/3 operating profit: IFIS consensus ¥163,957m (ordinary ¥154,195m, unchanged for 4 weeks) vs company plan ¥150,000m (ordinary ¥137,000m), https://kabuyoho.jp/reportAnalyst?bcode=9202 (read 2026-10-29) and the Q1 決算短信 https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260729/140120260729501430.pdf. H1 cumulative ordinary consensus ¥69,957m (same kabuyoho page). print_vs_bar is my estimate of the revised FY OP guide (~¥140-150bn) against the ¥164bn consensus; one estimate source plus the company plan, so the bar is only partly sourced and sizes are kept small.
positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register (baseline, as of 2026-10-28, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html): 3.42% across 3 sellers, +0.08pt vs prior, i.e. mildly building, not crowded. Part of it may be hedges against the 2031 euro-yen convertible bond (conversion-price adjustment notice 2026-06-26 on https://irbank.net/9202/ir), so the baseline's short_squeeze lean (+2.05) likely overstates squeeze fuel. 信用倍率 4.75 (baseline; also shown on https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=9202 on 2026-10-29): margin longs crowded, which is the setup in which a visible negative still has sellers. No options, no skew. Run-up -5.15% 20d, -2.18% 5d; price ~2,846 vs 3,221 on the Q1 release day.

findings.finding: The FY plan (OP ¥150bn) assumes Singapore kerosene of $120 in Q2 and $90 in 2H (Dubai $100/$75), but ANA's own surcharge filing puts the Aug-Sep kerosene average at ¥25,000-26,000/bbl (~$160) and the Q1 deck said 'Q2 trends will be reflected in the 2H assumptions'; using the plan's own implied sensitivity (~¥1,400億 for a +$40 average, ≈¥35億 per $1 per year) a re-based 2H costs roughly ¥240-390億 net of surcharge/hedge recovery against a Q1 cushion of +¥290億, so a trim of the ¥150bn plan toward ¥130-145bn is more likely than a hold, against a consensus of ¥164bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Close-to-close after 15:30 releases: 2026-04-30 first guide OP -31% on oil -> +4.15% (relief); 2025-10-30 H1 with upward revision -> +4.05%; 2026-07-29 Q1 beating internal plan by ¥290億 but plan held -> -2.11% after a +2.58% run into the print; 2025-07-29 -> -4.08%. Bad guides have been bought when the stock had already sold off (computed from https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/9202.T?range=2y&interval=1d).
findings.why_not_priced: The oil path is public and the stock is ~12% below its Q1-release close, so part of a cut is held; but the IFIS consensus has not moved in four weeks and still sits 9% ABOVE the company plan, which is not what a consensus that had marked 2H fuel to ~$160 would look like. The headline a cut produces (下方修正 vs a consensus above plan) is what the crowded margin long (4.75x) has not yet been handed.
findings.independence: Fuel level: travel.watch on ANA's 11-12月 surcharge (Aug-Sep average ¥25-26k/bbl, Jun-Jul table ¥20-21k), https://travel.watch.impress.co.jp/docs/news/2148470.html, 2026-10-15. Plan assumptions also in the April deck https://www.ana.co.jp/group/investors/data/kessan/pdf/2026_04_2.pdf. The Q1 cushion (+¥290億 vs internal plan, Middle East hit halved, coverage 55%) is in the SAME Q1 deck and is netted inside this finding rather than filed as a second, opposite-signed one.

findings.finding: ANA's international traffic growth decelerated through Q2 (passengers +13.2% June, +7.9% July, +1.3% August with LF -1.4pt and Asia/Oceania below last year) and domestic fell for a third month (-6.9% in August, LF -3.2pt), so the revenue engine that produced Q1's +¥190億 revenue beat against plan was weaker in the summer peak quarter that carries most of H1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: revenue record and plan beat -> stock -2.11% next session; reported-quarter beats have not been bought on their own.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the monthly traffic is public (LESSONS rule 1). What is left is that H1 consensus ordinary of ¥69,957m implies Q2 ordinary ~¥47bn (-20% YoY) when Q1 fell 37% with weaker fuel YoY; cargo (AI demand, not visible monthly) could cover it, so this is small.
findings.independence: July figures: https://www.aviationwire.jp/archives/350531 (2026-09-15). Same publisher, different month; one series, counted once.

findings.finding: The ¥150bn buyback (to 2026-12-15) was 84% done by 30 September (¥125.5bn, 42.34m shares), and the 2026-2028 strategy states an additional buyback is under consideration during the plan period subject to financial-health targets and funding conditions, so a new authorisation announced with the H1 batch is a live, low-probability upside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The current programme was announced 2025-11-10 at 16:00, separately from the H1 results, together with a hybrid preferred issuance to fund it; no buyback has been announced in an H1 TDnet batch in the irbank record since 2022.
findings.why_not_priced: A stock at PBR 0.89 with a crowded margin long would carry a premium if a new programme were expected; nothing in the tape or the news flow suggests one is anticipated, and an oil-shock profit year makes it less likely, which is why the expected value is small.
findings.independence: Policy wording '本戦略期間において追加の自己株式取得を検討' in the individual-investor briefing https://www.ana.co.jp/group/investors/individual/pdf/briefing_materials_2603.pdf (2026-03).

baseline_tension: The baseline's priced lean is +1.81 (mostly a short-squeeze term that a CB-hedged 3.4% short register probably overstates) and the run-up is -5%; my findings lean slightly negative against it. The strongest positive the release could carry is a HELD ¥150bn plan on the strength of the +¥290億 Q1 cushion and surcharge recovery, or a new buyback; I looked for both and they keep p_up at 45 rather than lower, together with April's +4.15% on a -31% guide.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (negative resting on a public monthly series): the traffic-deceleration finding cut from -0.4 to -0.2, and p_up moved from 44 to 45; the guidance finding left at -1.2 because the release is expected to ADD a forecast change.
Rule 2 (check the sign): the strongest positives (held plan on the Q1 cushion, new buyback) were searched and are carried as the netted cushion in finding 1 and as finding 3; no further change.
